gates.name: Production reachability
gates.blocker: The complete normal sealed flow passes locally; the pushed Pages deployment still needs the same visible end-to-end replay.

gates.name: Input parity
gates.blocker: POINTER AND KEYBOARD reach the canonical world for all five accepted starter fixtures ON DESKTOP: each click and each Enter increments that fixture's own interaction count and records its own action, measured per interaction against a freshly read rectangle. HOVER HOLDS TOO: hovering accepted ink changes both the cursor and the fixture's own presentation, and reverts when the pointer leaves. TOUCH DOES NOT: at 390x844 the stepping stones and the planter have no interaction rectangle, and a full-width drag does not move the camera, so nothing brings them into reach -- a strict expected failure in tests/test_garden_review_e2e_browser.py. Terminal parity unaffected by this work. (Corrected four times on 2026-08-03, every one my own error: this entry first said four of five fixtures ignore a click and keyboard reaches nothing; then that touch reaches all five, which the mobile expected failure contradicts; then that hover was uncovered; then that hover changes only the cursor, which was an artifact of measuring under `garden_review_time` -- the review clock freezes presentation, so the renderer never repainted the emphasis it had already computed. See docs/FAILURE_LOG.md.)

gates.name: Standalone value
gates.blocker: The implemented standalone glance, tend, and dwell loops require direct human usefulness observation.

gates.name: Atlas portability
gates.blocker: The single manifest and width/grapheme validation pass, but the supported browser/terminal screenshot matrix for tofu, overlap, and frame jitter remains.

gates.name: Parallax and performance
gates.blocker: Per-object parallax, inverse hit testing, deterministic rate, ten-minute pan, and partial diffs pass; reference desktop/mobile p95 frame-time measurements remain.

gates.name: Accessibility
gates.blocker: Reduced motion, 200% zoom and the 44px floor now hold in a real browser, and so does keyboard play on the product path: ']' walks canonical focus through all five accepted starter fixtures and Enter performs each one's declared primary action, proved against canonical world state and against three mutations of the viewer. NARROW LAYOUT DOES NOT: at 390x844 the stepping stones and planter have no interaction rectangle at all. SPATIAL FOCUS IS HALF DONE: move_focus now resolves left/right/up/down to the nearest object in that direction by canonical position, identically in both engines across all 28 object-direction cases and mutation-proved; but the browser still binds the arrow keys to pan, so no direction ever reaches the command from a keyboard. What the arrows should do when they can no longer both pan and navigate is an unmade product decision. Both are strict expected failures in tests/test_garden_review_e2e_browser.py. VoiceOver/NVDA and no-color still require human observation. (Corrected 2026-08-03 twice: this entry first claimed target sizing and narrow layout pass, which the browser E2E disproved; it then claimed every target is 15x17 px and that keyboard play is impossible, both of which were my own measurement errors and are disproved by the executed keyboard and 44px tests.)

gates.name: Human acceptance
gates.blocker: Direct human sign-off cannot be replaced by code, fixtures, or agent observation.
